title.en: Two things that must be searched for

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that reads 'Dirshu Hashem b'himatzo' as the ten days from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, when Hashem is especially accessible. He links this to the Beis HaMikdash, whose site the Torah left for Yidden to search out, as David HaMelech swore not to sleep until he found it.

title.en: The Mikdash as the world's point of origin

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the Gemara that the Mikdash is 'higher' than Eretz Yisrael: not physically, but as the point on the globe where creation began, the Even Shesiyah and the center of habitation. He explains Har as herayon, conception, and adds that thought, hirhur, comes even before it, like an architect's plan before the building.

title.en: Olam, shanah, nefesh and the forty days

summary.en: Bringing the Sefer Yetzirah's triad of olam, shanah and nefesh, the Mashgiach shows that each has a Kodesh HaKodashim, joined when the Kohen Gadol enters the Kodesh HaKodashim on Yom Kippur. He compares the forty days of an embryo's formation to the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul to Yom Kippur, and says that climbing the 'Har Hashem' of Rosh Hashanah requires preparation from Rosh Chodesh Elul.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Adam HaRishon

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that Rosh Hashanah is in time what Yerushalayim is in place, the gate of heaven where tefillos rise, and that the Even Shesiyah contains the whole world as Rosh Hashanah contains the whole year. Yom Kippur is hirhur, beyond herayon, and Adam HaRishon, the origin of all mankind, was formed from the place of the Mikdash, uniting the three origins.

The Mashgiach explains that David HaMelech carries the neshamah of Adam HaRishon and of Moshiach, and that an origin is hard to find because it begins in thought. He shows this from Shmuel, who did not recognize David among Yishai's sons; from David and Shmuel, who first chose the wrong site for the Mikdash; and from the Gemara's story of the Levi'im who erred about whether it was Rosh Hashanah.

The Mashgiach brings the zaken mamre, who is liable only when the Sanhedrin sits in the place of the Mikdash, because Torah goes forth from Tziyon. Torah is the blueprint of the world, as he illustrates with the Chazon Ish guiding surgeons from the Torah, so Yerushalayim, the center of the world, should be found in the middle of the Torah, and he looks for it in the middle of Sefer Devarim.

The Mashgiach explains that in the ten days of teshuvah Hashem tells Yidden to create the world and themselves: through the shofar a new neshamah is blown in, and the ten pesukim of each of Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofros correspond to the ten utterances of creation. He calls for searching Hashem, the Mikdash and Moshiach, and, like David who was up at night, for not sleeping, bringing the Yerushalmi, Rashi on Yaakov's sleep and the Rambam on the shofar.

The Mashgiach says that reaching the peak is not automatic: one can tear off calendar pages and arrive at Rosh Hashanah still at the bottom of the mountain. He speaks of the last generation, 'zeh dor dorshav', who will search for and find Hashem and crown Him, and closes with a call for teshuvah and tzedakah for poor children's Torah learning and with brachos.

oneLiner.en: At the seudah of Purim Hameshulash the Mashgiach teaches that the joy of Purim is that a Jew remains a Jew in every state, and that the holy point in every Jew stays fresh and can never be extinguished.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach speaks at the seudah of Purim Hameshulash, when Purim in Yerushalayim meets Shabbos. He explains that Purim belongs to the weekday: as the Chiddushei HaRim teaches, Purim and Chanukah strengthen Jews in their weekday state, and the 'days of feasting and joy' are the joy that one has remained a Jew. From the halachah that a town near Yerushalayim and visible from it counts as Yerushalayim, he learns that even Jews who fell outside the camp, whom Amalek attacked, still belong. Haman called the Jews 'asleep from the mitzvos', old and stale, and the blasphemer mocked the lechem hapanim as stale bread; but the lechem hapanim stayed fresh, and so does the spark in every Jew. He explains that the wine at Achashverosh's feast was the sealed wine prepared for the nesachim, and closes with the gates of Gan Eden that open when the Megillah is read.

en: The 'days of feasting and joy' of Purim are the joy that one has remained a Jew, whatever one's state.
Purim belongs to the weekday and cannot fall on Shabbos, because it strengthens Jews in their weekday state.
The essence of Torah is the point of Jewishness, that a Jew remains a Jew; Amalek attached itself even to the Jews who had fallen outside the camp.
Haman called the Jews 'asleep from the mitzvos', old and cold, but Jews stay fresh like the lechem hapanim, and the fire in every Jewish heart cannot be put out.
The wine served at Achashverosh's feast was the sealed wine the Kohanim had prepared for the nesachim, and it carried their holiness.
The Megillah is the point of Jewishness, and when it is read the gates of Gan Eden open.

candidateTopics: Purim as a weekday Yom Tov

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens his words at the seudah and speaks about the idea of a chok.
An interlude.

title.en: Mordechai's crown and Purim in Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach mentions Mordechai and the crown of rulership, and then turns to Yerushalayim, where this year Purim meets Shabbos and the seudah is eaten on another day.
The Mashgiach speaks about Shabbos and about what goes from it into the weekdays, and says that a day merits to carry holiness into the weekday.
An interlude.

title.en: Like a mikveh, Purim makes a Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Purim to a mikveh, which can make a Jew out of a non-Jew, and speaks of awakening the holy point in the heart so that one takes oneself to avodas Hashem.
An interlude.

title.en: Near and visible: every Jew belongs

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the halachah that a town near Yerushalayim and visible from it is counted with it, and learns from it that a Jew remains a Jew, even those who fell outside the camp whom Amalek attacked. He brings the Chiddushei HaRim that Purim strengthens Jews in the weekday, and explains the 'days of feasting and joy' as the joy of remaining a Jew.
An interlude.

title.en: Asleep from the mitzvos, fresh like the lechem hapanim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that 'yeshainim', sleeping, also means old, and that one who sleeps at the mitzvos has grown old. He brings the blasphemer's mockery of the lechem hapanim as stale bread, and answers that it stayed fresh; this was the coldness of Amalek, while the spark in every Jew stays fresh forever.

title.en: The wine of the nesachim at Achashverosh's feast

summary.en: After singing, the Mashgiach asks how every guest at Achashverosh's feast could be served wine older than himself when Eretz Yisrael lay desolate, and answers that it was the sealed wine prepared in the Beis Hamikdash for the nesachim. With a story of fish prepared while singing Nishmas, he explains that this wine carried holiness, and that this led to the decree on Vashti and to Esther's coming.

title.en: The gates of Gan Eden open on Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a soul that revealed that souls wait at a gate of Gan Eden until Purim, when the Megillah is read and the gates open. He explains that the Megillah is the point of Jewishness, and the gates open for every Jew.

title.en: At the point, all Jews are equal

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that while Jews differ in greatness and honor, at the inner point all Jews are equal, and the joy of Purim belongs to all of them. He asks with what merit we merited Purim Hameshulash, and speaks of teshuvah.
The Mashgiach explains that the word of return refers to teshuvah, and continues with words about the end of Rome's rule.

The Mashgiach speaks of Mordechai and of the pride of a Jew, which the Torah gives him. He explains that Torah and Yisrael are one, that every Jew has a bond with Torah, and that even when some have gone away, their children can still learn Torah.
An interlude.

title.en: The Jews outside the camp belong to Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the halachah of walled cities and to the Jews who fell away from the camp: three and a half thousand years later Amalek still attaches itself to them. Though some call them sinful Jews, he says they belong to Yerushalayim and must be supported.
The close of the seudah.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah of a yovel year, the Mashgiach explains Purim as the joy of chasan and kallah: Hashem comes down to Klal Yisrael even in its lowest state, hidden in nature, and Shushan Purim binds the Jews to Yerushalayim and to malchus beis Dovid.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the war against Amalek, which the Alshich explains as the daily war against the yetzer hara, and with the call to gather and accept malchus shamayim. Purim, unlike other yomim tovim, is Hashem coming down into nature; with the Ramban he teaches that everything is hashgachah, and shows Haman himself preparing the salvation. He tells of gedolim pressed by Czar Nicholas to sign a blank paper. Purim's miracle came in a yovel year, as does this year; yovel is reunion, like the joy of chasan and kallah, and the Megillah shows Hashem coming to His kallah even in the tannery. The second part treats Haman's descendants who taught Torah, the spark in Amalek, the rejection of malchus beis Dovid and its tikkun through Mordechai and Shushan Purim, Esther's request for a 'tomorrow', and the last days of the yovel year.

en: On other yomim tovim a Jew rises toward heaven; on Purim Hashem comes down into nature, so the Megillah tells of events with no open miracle, all guided by hashgachah.
The Megillah proclaims to the lowest generations, before Moshiach and in hester panim, that Ribono shel Olam runs the world.
The miracle of Purim came in a yovel year, and this year too is a yovel year; yovel means returning and reuniting, the root of the joy of chasan and kallah.
On Purim Hashem comes to Klal Yisrael like a chasan to his kallah, even to the lowest place, and knocks on each Jew's door asking to be let in.
Purim repaired the earlier rejection of malchus shamayim, malchus beis Dovid and the Beis HaMikdash; Shushan Purim, which Esther requested, binds the Jews to Yerushalayim.
Yehoshua only weakened Amalek because a spark of holiness lies hidden in it, which must come out.

candidateTopics: Hashem and Klal Yisrael as chasan and kallah

summary.en: The opening of the seudah.

title.en: The war against Amalek and the wine of the sar hamashkim

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the Jews standing up against Amalek and brings the Alshich that wiping out Amalek means nullifying the yetzer hara, a war renewed every moment. He turns to Yosef and the sar hamashkim's dream of the wine, and calls on all to gather, accept malchus shamayim and bind themselves to Yerushalayim.
Singing.

The Mashgiach explains that on Purim Hashem comes down into nature, brings the Ramban that everything that happens to a Jew is hashgachah, and shows from the Gemara that Haman, as Memuchan, himself prepared the salvation. The Megillah proclaims to the last generations that Hashem runs the world.

title.en: The gedolim and the czar's blank paper

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Czar Nicholas summoned three gedolim of Russia and demanded that they sign a blank sheet on which he would write what he wished, and how one of them stood firm and refused, ready to be killed rather than give in.

title.en: Purim, yovel and the joy of chasan and kallah

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that the miracle of Purim came in a yovel year and that Mordechai is hinted in the word 'deror', the freedom of yovel. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya that chasan and kallah were one soul divided in two, so their reunion brings great joy, and explains that this reunion is the meaning of yovel, which falls this year.

The Mashgiach explains that the Megillah brings Jews back as in yovel, and that Mordechai's soul is a soul of yovel. From the pasuk 'lo me'astim' that the Gemara applies to the days of Haman, he reads 'lechalosam' as 'kallah': Hashem, like a king's son, comes to His kallah even in a tannery, which is the joy of Purim in exile.

title.en: The Chasan knocks at the door

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties the Purim gathering to Yerushalayim and Shushan Purim, notes that this seudah is also a sheva brachos with a chasan present, and likens Purim to Yom Kippur. He says the most fallen souls have the greatest share in Purim, for Hashem comes to the lowest place, knocks and asks each Jew to open for Him.
An interlude at the end of the first part.

title.en: Timna, Haman's descendants and the spark in Amalek

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Haman's descendants who taught Torah in Bnei Brak and brings the Gemara about Timna, who wanted to join the house of Yaakov and became the mother of Amalek. Her small desire bore fruit thousands of years later. Yehoshua only weakened Amalek because a spark lies hidden in it.

title.en: Shaul, the Arizal and raising the hidden sparks

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Shaul's words 'I have fulfilled the word of Hashem' in connection with the spark in Amalek, and the Arizal's teaching that drinking on Purim raises the sparks hidden in Haman. He adds that a spark of holiness lies hidden in every place.
An interlude.

title.en: Rejecting malchus beis Dovid and Achashverosh's feast

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that after Shlomo HaMelech's death the Jews rejected malchus shamayim, malchus beis Dovid and the Beis HaMikdash, and will see blessing only when they seek all three again. He then brings the Gemara that Achashverosh calculated the seventy years, thought there would be no more Beis HaMikdash, and made his feast with its vessels, and the Jews attended.

title.en: Two Purims: the world and Shushan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Purim was a tikkun for that sin. There are two Purims: one for the Jews of the whole world, for whom the decree turned to joy, and Shushan Purim, which Esther asked for with 'yinasen gam machar', a tikkun for the rejection of malchus beis Dovid and bound up with the joy of Yerushalayim.

title.en: Mordechai, Dovid HaMelech and longing for Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Mordechai, from Binyamin, was moser nefesh to acknowledge Dovid HaMelech and so repaired the sin of his ancestor Shimi. Though we are not in Yerushalayim, with our longing for it we join the joy of Shushan Purim; Mordechai never forgot Yerushalayim.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach explains that where a Jew's thought is, there he is, in place and in time. Esther's request 'yinasen gam machar' was a plea for a tomorrow: a day when Jews serve in the Beis HaMikdash, the coming of Moshiach ben Dovid.
An interlude.

title.en: From Purim to Pesach: the last days of the yovel year

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that every night from Purim to Pesach Hashem takes a Jew out of the gates of tumah into the gates of kedushah. Standing at the end of the yovel year, in the second Adar, he says the last days of the month should be days of avodas Hashem, learning and davening with effort, and asks that they bring nachas ruach to Hashem.
The close of the seudah, with the sheva brachos.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Purim reveals the Kodesh HaKodashim hidden in every Jew, that the Megillah is Hashem's letter to each Jew, written in heaven and belonging to the days of Moshiach, and that its salvation, reached through simcha, reaches our own times.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by speaking of the secrets of Purim and of preparing for Moshiach. He explains that Amalek, 'the first of the nations', aimed at the Kodesh HaKodashim, and that every Jew carries a Kodesh HaKodashim that no sin reaches; Purim is the day of that inner sanctuary, which is why one is not exacting with Purim money. He explains the custom of spreading the Megillah like a letter: the end is seen from the start, and emunah means knowing in the middle of events that all is for good, reading Hashem's Megillah in the world and in one's own life. He develops the Gemara on the Megillah's ruach hakodesh, with the Hafla'ah on Rabbi Meir and Shmuel's 'they upheld above', and says the Megillah belongs to the days of Moshiach. He closes with Mordechai's heel, the Megillah as a letter to the lowest Jew, Achashveirosh and Yishmael, and salvation through simcha.

en: Every Jew carries a Kodesh HaKodashim within him that is never defiled, even in the greatest rasha, and Purim is the day of that Kodesh HaKodashim; its joy is rejoicing with it.
One is not exacting with Purim money because on Purim the point of holiness in every Jew is revealed: a Jew is a Jew, and one does not examine him.

The Megillah is spread out like a letter before it is read because its end is known from the start; emunah means knowing in the middle of events, before the end is seen, that all Hashem does is for the good of the Jews.
Every 'the king' in the Megillah refers to the Ribono shel Olam, and a Jew must read Hashem's Megillah in the events of the world and of his own life as one plan of hashgacha pratis.
The Megillah is written above in heaven; this is Shmuel's 'they upheld above what they accepted below', and even simple Jews feel that it was written with ruach hakodesh.
The Megillah belongs to the days of Moshiach, which is why it will not be nullified when other books are, and why its light is so great.

Hashem brought the Purim miracle through a king of Persia to hint that in the time before Moshiach the klipah of Yishmael will be subdued, and the salvation of today comes through the power of Purim's simcha.

candidateTopics: the Kodesh HaKodashim within every Jew
the Megillah and the days of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling the secrets of Purim a great thing, to be approached with simcha. He recalls that the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah at first did not accept the Megillah until Hashem enlightened their eyes, and greets all who have gathered.

title.en: Preparing for Moshiach; Amalek against holiness

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that Moshiach can come soon and one must prepare to greet him with a holy joy. He then explains that Amalek, 'the first of the nations', includes all the nations, that Haman aimed to rule over the Kodesh HaKodashim, and that Amalek was only weakened by Yehoshua and will be fully uprooted only by Moshiach.

title.en: The Kodesh HaKodashim in every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew is a Beis HaMikdash and his inner point is a Kodesh HaKodashim that no sin reaches, even in the greatest rasha. Purim is therefore the day of the Kodesh HaKodashim, like Yom Kippur; Haman's war was against it, and the joy of Purim is rejoicing that it was never defiled. He brings the Emrei Emes on 'these days are remembered and done'.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach asks why the Shulchan Aruch rules that one is not exacting with Purim money but gives to whoever stretches out a hand. He answers that on Purim the point of holiness in every Jew is revealed: a Jew is a Jew, and the favor every Jew has before Hashem shines. He adds that a Jew should know on Purim that he is born anew.
Singing.

title.en: The Megillah as a letter: seeing the end from the start

summary.en: From the rule that one who reads the Megillah out of order is not yotzei and the custom to spread it out like a letter, the Mashgiach teaches that the end is known from the start, and that emunah means knowing during events that all is for good. Every 'the king' in the Megillah means Hashem, and a Jew must read Hashem's Megillah in the world and in his own life.
Singing.

title.en: Was the Megillah said with ruach hakodesh?

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah found the Megillah hinted in 'write this as a remembrance in the book', and the proofs of Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva that it was said with ruach hakodesh. He marvels that Shmuel, an Amora, claims a better proof than three generations of the greatest Tannaim, and explains how the Tannaim's proofs show that every word was dictated from heaven.

title.en: Rabbi Meir's Megillah and Shmuel's proof

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Rabbi Meir wrote a Megillah from memory although one may not write from memory, and the Hafla'ah's explanation: the Torah is written in heaven at its root, and Rabbi Meir looked into the root and copied from it. On this he explains Shmuel: the Tannaim could see the Megillah written above, but hid their level and brought proofs from pesukim.

title.en: Every Jew feels it; the inner eye

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every Jew, even a child or a simple worker, feels that the Megillah was written with ruach hakodesh, since through the Purim miracle a light of emunah came down. Yet the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah could not see it in heaven, for it was hidden too high. He brings the Gemara calling the prophets 'tzofim' and the Rambam on the hidden aron, and explains that great tzaddikim see with an inner eye.

title.en: The Megillah belongs to the days of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the prophets could not see the Megillah in heaven because it belongs to the world of Moshiach, until Hashem gave them a new light and they saw that 'in the book' means the Megillah. Its light is a light of the days of Moshiach: as the Rambam writes it will never be nullified, and the Chasam Sofer says its light is greater than that of the Torah of Moshe.

title.en: Mordechai's heel and the footsteps of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Mordechai climbed onto Haman to mount the horse and kicked him, answering with 'and you shall tread upon their high places'. He explains that this, Moshe Rabbeinu's last words to the Jews, corresponds to ikvesa d'Meshicha, the generation of the heel, and that Mordechai is a spark of Moshe Rabbeinu.

title.en: A letter addressed to the lowest Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a letter, unlike a book, comes with an address: Mordechai wrote the Megillah for every Jew, and it lies in every Jew's mailbox. Citing the Tanya that even the lowest Jew is bound with the Ein Sof, he says 'this letter of Purim' was written for the lowest Jew, and connects Purim with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Lag Ba'Omer.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer's answer to how Achashveirosh, son of a king of Persia, bought the throne when by rotation it belonged to Madai. He then brings the Abarbanel's question why Yishmael is missing from the four kingdoms, and his answer that Paras alludes to Yishmael: Hashem brought the miracle through a Persian king as a sign that Yishmael will be subdued before Moshiach.

The Mashgiach says the Megillah was written for all generations, and the salvation needed today comes through the power of Purim's simcha. He tells of a tzaddik in Amsterdam who, in a time of danger on Purim, sat drinking with his people instead of davening, because on Purim one achieves with simcha what all year is achieved with tefillah and fasting. He closes that salvation comes only from Hashem and calls for emunah and bitachon.
Singing.

title.en: Ahavas Yisrael and Purim as Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the secret of ahavas Yisrael from the Tanya: bodies are separate but souls are united. He connects Purim with Shabbos and with the future day that will be entirely Shabbos.
Singing.

title.en: A wall of fire; Achashveirosh's imitation

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Yerushalayim in the time of Moshiach, which will need no wall because Hashem will be a wall of fire around it, and ties this to the days of Mordechai and Esther. He brings the Midrash that Achashveirosh imitated the Beis HaMikdash in his palace garden.
Singing.

catalogTitle: Chanukah Mashiach ben Yosef and ben David

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Chanukah light is the hidden light of Moshiach, which reaches even the most distant Jewish souls, and shows how Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David came into the world through people whose greatness was concealed.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Me'or Einayim on the Gemara that wicks and oils unfit for Shabbos may be used for Chanukah, and with the Rokeach, brought by the Bnei Yissaschar, that the hidden light of creation is revealed on Chanukah. Hashem's candles are the souls of Jews. Shabbos lights stay above ten tefachim, but the Chanukah light is lit in the public domain, below ten tefachim, on the left side, at the dark end of the month, to rekindle souls lost in the domain of the Sitra Achra. Every Jew has a hidden love for Hashem that Chanukah brings out. He then finds the light of Moshiach in Vayeshev and Miketz: Yosef and Yehuda, Tamar, Osnas, Dina and even Shechem carried a hidden spark of Moshiach that no one recognized. He closes that just as Yosef suddenly revealed himself to his brothers, a moment will come when the light of Moshiach answers every question.

en: According to the Rokeach, the hidden light of creation is revealed on Chanukah, each person according to his level, and it is the light of Moshiach.
The Mashgiach explains that Hashem's candles are the souls of Jews, and the Chanukah light is lit below ten tefachim in the public domain to rekindle souls that are in the domain of the Sitra Achra.
Wicks too weak for Shabbos burn on Chanukah: souls too far for Shabbos to reach can still be awakened by Chanukah.
Every Jew has a hidden love for Hashem, a spark that can never be extinguished, and Chanukah is a time that brings it out.
Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David both come through hidden lights: Yosef, Yehuda, Tamar, Osnas and Dina, whose true greatness was not recognized.
Just as the brothers suddenly understood Yosef when he said 'I am Yosef', a moment will come when the light of Moshiach is revealed and all questions on Hashem's ways are answered.

candidateTopics: Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David

title.en: Wicks for Chanukah and the hidden light

summary.en: After thanking his hosts, the Mashgiach brings the Me'or Einayim on the Gemara that wicks and oils unfit for Shabbos may be lit on Chanukah, and the Rokeach that the hidden light of creation is revealed on Chanukah. He adds that Hashem too has candles: the souls of Jews, whose brightness is concealed.

title.en: Below ten tefachim in the public domain

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the public domain as the domain of the Sitra Achra, and brings the Gemara that the Shechinah never descended below ten tefachim, except on Chanukah, whose light is lit at the door, below ten tefachim and on the left side. These lights are Jewish souls who do not properly accept the yoke of Heaven and must be rekindled.

title.en: Light at the dark end of the month

summary.en: Unlike the other Yomim Tovim, which come with a full or growing moon, Chanukah comes at the end of the month in the longest nights. The Mashgiach notes that even Jews who do not keep Shabbos light Chanukah candles, and explains that our kindling below arouses Hashem, like a shadow, to kindle these souls with the light of Moshiach and bring them to teshuvah.

title.en: Eight strings and the hidden love

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the harp in the Beis HaMikdash had seven strings and that of Moshiach will have eight, so Chanukah's eight days are the light of Moshiach. Every Jew has a hidden love for Hashem that Chanukah brings out, and he returns to the Me'or Einayim: wicks Shabbos cannot ignite, Chanukah can.

title.en: Two Mashiachs in Vayeshev and Miketz

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash at the start of Vayeshev that while everyone was busy with his own concerns, the light of Moshiach was being created, and the Gemara and Zohar on the two Mashiachs, ben Yosef and ben David. Yosef was a hidden light his brothers did not recognize, and there was also a time they did not recognize who Yehuda was.

Yehuda, once leader of the Shevatim, went down from his brothers; both he and Yosef descended below their level to bring Moshiach. Tamar carried the spark of Moshiach ben David and was taken for a zonah, and the Mashgiach tells from the Targum Yonasan and the Midrash how Osnas, daughter of Dina and Shechem, reached Egypt and carried the spark of Moshiach ben Yosef.

title.en: The 'tyrant' and the diamond in Shechem

summary.en: The brothers saw Yosef as a tyrant until he said 'I am Yosef'. The Mashgiach then explains that Shechem himself held a spark of Moshiach ben Yosef, hidden in him like a diamond hidden in a garbage can, and that what befell Dina was planned from Above so this spark could unite with hers.

The Mashgiach shows that Dina was born with the spark of Moshiach, hinted in her name: spelled out with the full letter names, Dina equals the gematria of Moshiach ben Yosef. He returns to Yehuda's going down and to Tamar, a tzaddekes who risked her life to bring Moshiach and was so concealed that she appeared as a zonah.

title.en: The moment when everything is revealed

summary.en: In one moment Yosef stopped being the tyrant and Tamar was revealed as more righteous than Yehuda. The Mashgiach closes that Jews today ask why they suffer and why Hashem is silent, but a moment will come, like 'I am Yosef', when the light of Moshiach, the light of Chanukah, will be revealed and answer every question.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Amalek's chutzpah and doubt are overcome through humility, love of every Jew and emunah, and that the sin behind Haman's decree was giving up hope for Moshiach and Yerushalayim, so the tikkun of Purim is to believe in and long for the redemption.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by warning that the great day of Purim must not be lost in the bustle of mishloach manos. Amalek is the klipah of chutzpah, and Moshe Rabbeinu fought him with humility, telling his student Yehoshua 'choose for us'; mishloach manos, sent by the greater to the smaller, carries the same humility and the unity of Klal Yisrael. Amalek is also the klipah of doubt, and its holy counterpart is Teveria, whose status is itself a doubt, which is why Moshiach will come there first. The decree of Haman came because the Jews bowed to Nevuchadnetzar's image and joined Achashverosh's feast, both a denial that Bavel would fall and that the Beis HaMikdash would be rebuilt. The tikkun of Purim is to believe in Moshiach and rejoice in Yerushalayim. In the second part he explains that Amalek has no future, that every Jew keeps Avraham's root, and that Purim is a time to ask for the redemption.

en: Purim is a great time in which one can merit the highest things, so one must ask Hashem not to lose the day in the bustle of mishloach manos.
Amalek is the klipah of chutzpah, and the war against him is fought with humility, honoring the smaller one and unity among Jews.
The Jews of that generation deserved destruction because bowing to the image and joining Achashverosh's feast both meant denying the coming of Moshiach and the rebuilding of Yerushalayim.
The tikkun of Purim is to believe that Moshiach will come and that Jews will return to Yerushalayim, and to rejoice in the joy of Yerushalayim.
On Purim the hidden root of every Jew, bound to Hashem, is revealed, so every Jew can rejoice even when his cheshbon hanefesh shows him his faults.
Every Jew carries the beginning of Klal Yisrael, Avraham Avinu, which cannot be nullified, while Amalek, whose beginning is evil, has no future.

candidateTopics: hidden root of the Jewish soul

title.en: Not losing the great day of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns that the day can be lost in the rush of mishloach manos, and says one must ask Hashem to merit the great time of Purim, keeping it with seriousness and with joy and giving nachas ruach to Hashem.

title.en: 'Choose for us': humility against Amalek's chutzpah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Amalek is the klipah of chutzpah, a rebel who knows his Master, and that Moshe fought him with humility by making his student Yehoshua his equal. In the time before Moshiach, when chutzpah grows, the war against Amalek is through humility, and mishloach manos sent by the greater to the smaller carries this avodah.

title.en: Mishloach manos, unity and love of every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties mishloach manos to the unity of Klal Yisrael, rooted in Hashem's oneness. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya that one hates the evil in a Jew but loves the Jew, and Rabbi Akiva's 'great principle of the Torah', and explains that honoring a fellow Jew awakens the honor of Hashem.
An interlude.

title.en: The small aleph, Rabbi Akiva and Adar Sheni

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects the small aleph, the sign of Moshe's humility, with Rabbi Akiva, who reminded Moshe what he had made from the leftover silver of the Mishkan. He speaks of Adar Rishon and Adar Sheni, and says that the reading of the Megillah brings back those who feel outside the camp yet still rejoice.
Singing.

title.en: Purim reveals the hidden root of every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Purim revealed the hidden root by which every Jew believes in Hashem even when He is hidden in nature. Amalek knows there is a Master, but the test is to see Hashem guiding a world that seems to run by itself; Jews believe even in a time of hester panim.

The Mashgiach explains that Amalek is the klipah of doubt, and its counterpart in holiness is Teveria, about which the Gemara is in doubt whether it counts as a walled city. For this reason Moshiach will come first to Teveria and from there to Yerushalayim: in a doubt a Jew still believes and serves with joy. Teveria belongs to Naftali, the twelfth tribe, as Adar is the twelfth month.

The Mashgiach brings Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's answer that the Jews of that generation deserved destruction because they bowed to the image, and tells the story of Chananya, Mishael and Azarya. He asks: according to Tosafos the image was not true avodah zarah, so why was this so grave, and why did the decree come only seventy years later?

title.en: Achashverosh's feast and the hope for Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer that Achashverosh made his feast because he could not bear the rebuilding of the Beis HaMikdash, and the Gemara that he counted seventy years and erred. Jews who joined the feast celebrated that there would be no Beis HaMikdash and no Moshiach, denying malchus beis David and Yerushalayim, which a Jew must long for as a foundation of emunah.

title.en: Daniel's dream and the golden image

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells Nevuchadnetzar's dream in Daniel chapter two, the image of gold, silver, copper and iron broken by a stone, which Daniel explained as the kingdoms of exile followed by Moshiach. Nevuchadnetzar then made an image entirely of gold to cancel the dream, so bowing to it meant denying the coming of Moshiach, the same as going to Achashverosh's feast.

The Mashgiach explains that joining the feast seventy years later awakened the old sin of the image, bringing the decree. He brings the Rambam on the inner will of every Jew to explain the difference between bowing under blows and bowing freely. The decree came for not keeping 'and they will seek Hashem their G-d and David their king', so the tikkun of Purim is to believe in Moshiach and rejoice in Yerushalayim.

title.en: The thirteen 'ein bein' and the two goats

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Mishnah 'there is no difference between Adar Rishon and Adar Sheni', the first of thirteen mishnayos opening 'ein bein', and the two goats of Yom Kippur that must be equal, like Yaakov and Esav who look alike outside. At the hidden root all Jews are holy and bound to Hashem, so on Purim every Jew rejoices even when his cheshbon hanefesh shows him his faults.
Singing.

title.en: Beginning and end: why Amalek has no future

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every person and nation has a starting point that remains as it grows. The beginning of Klal Yisrael is the Avos, so every Jew has something of Avraham Avinu that cannot be nullified. At the end of days other nations will shake off their klipah and be repaired, but Amalek cannot, since his very beginning is evil: 'Amalek is the first of the nations, and his end is destruction'.

title.en: The Ramban's student and Hashem's care for every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Ramban's student who left the path and whom the Ramban showed that his name is hinted in Parshas Ha'azinu. He explains that Haman wanted to wipe out the Jews so they would have no future, but Hashem is personally responsible for every Jew and will bring each one close.

title.en: Haman's lot and the month of Adar

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the future of Klal Yisrael and of Haman, who rejoiced when his lot fell in Adar. He says every Jew should know how precious he is to Hashem.
An interlude.

title.en: Why the day is named for Haman's lots

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every Jew should accept the yoke of Torah and mitzvos with love. He asks why Shavuos, Pesach and Chanukah are not named after the people of their miracles, yet Purim is named after Haman's lots, and speaks of the claim made against Mordechai that he had provoked Haman.

title.en: A Jew's sacrifice and the power of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew who gave money he had set aside for himself to help another Jew, and was given from Heaven the gift of blessing Jews. Purim lifts every Jew each year to higher levels, to his hidden root, and on this day one can long and pray.

title.en: An eis ratzon to ask for the redemption

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects Adar and Mordechai with the revelation of Moshiach, and says that Purim is a great eis ratzon when one can ask Hashem to fulfill 'and they will seek Hashem their G-d and David their king': the kingship of Heaven, the kingship of the house of David and the Beis HaMikdash.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach explains that Esther stood 'opposite the king's house', facing Yerushalayim, and prayed toward it, knowing that this would annul Haman's decree. Daniel too was cast to the lions not for praying, which he could have hidden, but for insisting on praying at the open window facing Yerushalayim. Singing follows.
Singing.

title.en: The salvation of Purim reveals every Jew's bond

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that other salvations came through a certain merit, but the sin before Purim was not seeking Hashem, David and Yerushalayim, and still Hashem helped. This revealed that every Jew is bound to Hashem at his inner root, and the salvation reached even the scattered of Israel against all their enemies.
The Mashgiach gives blessings to people mentioned by name and cries out for Moshiach; the seudah then draws to a close with a short story.
Singing.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Purim reveals the hidden, inner bond of every Jew with Hashem, which no sin reaches, and that Shushan Purim carries the joy of Yerushalayim out to every Jew, even the one standing far outside its wall.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that on Purim a Jew should see how far he has drifted and still rejoice, because even in the lowest state, like the Jews of Shushan whose Jewishness was hidden, he remains bound to Hashem. Every Jew has two hearts: the heart of stone sins, while the heart of flesh stays bound to Hashem, as the Rambam explains about a person who is compelled until he says he wants. Hashem 'remembers that they are flesh', and Achashverosh's feast hints at Hashem showing the beauty of every Jew. He then explains that Haman's lot fell on Adar without his knowing that Moshe was also born then, and that every Jew carries a spark of Moshe. Achashverosh withheld 'up to half the kingdom', the Beis HaMikdash, yet Esther ruled 127 provinces in the merit of Sarah. Finally, Shushan Purim brings Yerushalayim's joy beyond its wall, as Zechariah foretold a Yerushalayim without walls, surrounded by a wall of fire.

en: Purim is a time for a Jew to see how far he has strayed and still rejoice, because even in the lowest state he remains bound to Hashem.
A Jew sins only with his 'heart of stone'; his true 'heart of flesh' stays bound to Hashem, and on Purim this hidden bond comes into the open.
Haman's lot fell on Adar because Moshe Rabbeinu died then, but he did not know that Moshe was also born then, and every Jew carries a spark of Moshe.
Esther ruled over 127 provinces in the merit of Sarah, who lived 127 years.
Shushan Purim carries the joy of Yerushalayim beyond its wall, to every Jew wherever he is.
In the future Yerushalayim will have no wall; Hashem Himself will be a wall of fire around it, and it will take in every Jew.

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the Jew with Amalek and says that on Purim a Jew should rejoice even when he sees how far he has strayed. Like the Jews of Shushan, whose Jewishness was hidden, he stays bound to Hashem, and Purim is a time to open his eyes and begin anew.
An interlude at the seudah.

title.en: The hidden bond and the two hearts

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew has a hidden bond with Hashem that becomes revealed on Purim, in a world of Klal Yisrael that no sin reaches. A Jew sins with his heart of stone, not with his true heart of flesh, and he contrasts the way this works on Yom Kippur with Purim.

title.en: The inner will, as the Rambam explains

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the Megillah is likened to the Torah, and brings the Rambam on one who is compelled until he says 'I want': the yetzer forces him, but the Jew himself, at his inner point, wants to do the will of Hashem.

title.en: Hashem remembers that they are flesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that on Purim a Jew should become acquainted with his inner point, his heart of flesh, and know that his sins did not cut him off from Hashem. He brings the passuk that Hashem 'remembers that they are flesh', and reads Achashverosh's display of 'the glory of his kingdom' as Hashem showing the beauty of every Jew, even the lowest; at every level a Jew should sing.
Singing.

title.en: Haman's lot and the birth of Moshe

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haman rejoiced when the lot fell on Adar, the month Moshe Rabbeinu died, but did not know that Moshe was also born on the seventh of Adar. Moshe passed away in a way that 'no man knows his burial place', and every Jew carries a spark of Moshe, through which the decree was overturned.

title.en: Up to half the kingdom: the Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses Achashverosh's offer of 'up to half the kingdom', which excluded the building of the Beis HaMikdash, though Esther had not even asked for it. He asks why Achashverosh felt he had lost half his kingdom and explains that Yerushalayim stands in the middle of the world.

The Mashgiach brings that Esther ruled over 127 provinces in the merit of Sarah's 127 years, something Achashverosh did not know. He describes Achashverosh realizing, when Esther revealed her lineage, why his kingdom was bound up with the Beis HaMikdash, and then speaks of Jews rejoicing in the joy of Yerushalayim.
An interlude at the seudah.

title.en: Shushan Purim and Zechariah's open Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Esther's request 'let it be given tomorrow too' made a day of rejoicing with Yerushalayim. He contrasts the limits of Yerushalayim's wall with Shiloh, and brings the prophecy of Zechariah: the angel measuring Yerushalayim is told it will be settled without walls, and Hashem will be a wall of fire around it.

The Mashgiach explains that Yerushalayim is the heart of the world, with room for every Jew from the Kohen Gadol to the lowest. Amalek attacked those who were outside the camp, and Shushan Purim takes Yerushalayim beyond its wall to them. He notes that Shushan had no wall and that Yerushalayim appears in Tanach as many times as the numerical value of Shushan.

The Mashgiach explains that Haman was a klipah of tzimtzum, constriction, that builds a wall and attaches itself to those outside it. In Shushan, the place of the greatest concealment, Yerushalayim was granted its joy, and he brings the Tanya that Jews far away should rejoice like a villager whom the king comes to visit.

The Mashgiach returns to the angel who went to measure Yerushalayim, asking whether one would set limits on it. When Moshiach comes the joy will be greater the lower the light descends, and he says Mordechai and Esther are the souls of this joy.

title.en: Why Esther asked for another day

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses a concern that Purim, like the great Yamim Tovim, might be drawn into the weekday of Tisha B'Av, and explains that Esther's request for another day tied Shushan Purim to Yerushalayim, so that its praise would spread through the whole world.
Singing at the seudah.

title.en: Songs of longing and a parting blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls spending Shushan Purim with songs of praise, longing for Yerushalayim and dveikus, each according to his level. He says a Jew should be content and thank Hashem, asks those present to stay and sing, and blesses them to see Yerushalayim rebuilt.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Purim is the day Hashem Himself comes down to the lowest and most forgotten Jews, reveals the hidden point in every Jew, and shows that the whole masked world is only a garment over the Ribono shel Olam.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Yisro, who came to Moshe so broken that he could not move and thereby brought about the mitzvah of visiting the sick; on Chanukah and Purim, weekday Yomim Tovim, Hashem Himself visits the sick. Mordechai, a soul of the highest level, lowered himself to netzach and hod for the Jews, which explains why the Gemara counts him 'after four' and 'after five'. Purim is the day of returning lost things: Esther is the soul of the lost and forgotten, of the camp of Dan, of the last letters of the Torah, and she wrote the Megillah for the lowly generations. The world is a masked world, and Achashverosh hints to Hashem. Moshe struck the Mitzri, Haman's root, because no one may attack even the lowest Jew. Esther brought the Shechinah and Yerushalayim into Shushan, and Purim reveals the hidden love and the hidden wine in every Jew.

en: Chanukah and Purim are weekday Yomim Tovim on which Hashem Himself comes down to visit the sick, the Jews who feel broken and far away.
Mordechai, a soul from the highest level, came down to netzach and hod for the sake of the Jews, which is why the Gemara counts him 'after four' and 'after five'.
Purim is a day of returning lost things: Esther is the soul of the lost and forgotten, and she wrote the Megillah for the lowest generations.
Everything a Jew sees in nature, history and his own life is a garment; inside is the Ribono shel Olam, and Achashverosh in the Megillah hints to Him.
Hashem does not allow anyone to attack even the lowest Jew, because every Jew has a hidden root where no sin reaches.
Esther drew the Shechinah and the Beis HaMikdash into Shushan; so too the Jews, sitting together at the seudah and longing for Yerushalayim, draw Yerushalayim to where they are.

summary.en: Before the shiur begins.

The Mashgiach tells how Yisro came to Moshe so broken that he could not move, and so brought about the mitzvah of visiting the sick. On Chanukah and Purim, weekday Yomim Tovim, Hashem Himself comes down to visit the sick, and Purim spelled in full equals 'the way they shall go in it'.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that part of the Sanhedrin separated from Mordechai, so that he is listed after four and later after five, and says that those who left did not grasp his greatness. He asks why the Gemara does not simply say that he was fifth and then sixth.

title.en: Mor dror, tzori and the humble leader

summary.en: Mor dror heads the spices of the anointing oil, but in the ketores the tzori comes first. The Mashgiach contrasts leaders chosen for their gifts, like Moshe and David, with leaders chosen without reason, like Yiftach, reads 'Is there no balm in Gilad' on Yiftach, and explains Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's definition of tzori as the humility of a nasi seated at the head.

title.en: The hidden point where no sin reaches

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Noam Elimelech that there is a world called Klal Yisrael which no sin reaches, and the Chasam Sofer that beneath the skin all Jews are equal. Purim, for the last generations and the weakest Jews, reveals this point, as Yom Kippur reveals the 'I want' in every Jew.

title.en: Haman's slander, the Omer and Shushan Habirah

summary.en: Haman and Amalek slandered the purity of the Jews, and the Omer, brought like the offering of a sotah, attests that they are pure; so Mordechai taught the laws of the Omer. Shushan Habirah stands opposite the Beis HaMikdash, the peak of impurity against the peak of holiness, and Chanukah and Purim are netzach and hod, the two legs.

title.en: Mordechai descends to netzach and hod

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers his question: Mordechai, the mor dror at the head of the spices, came down to netzach and hod, to Chanukah and Purim, to visit the sick and the weak, and so the Gemara counts him after four and after five. He adds that the ketores, which stopped the plague, comes down to netzach and hod, and that mor is the fifth spice of the ketores.
Singing.

title.en: Purim and the mitzvah of returning lost things

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that Purim is the time of hashavas aveidah, made for the camp of Dan at the end of the camps, and that Esther is its soul. He brings the last verse of Tehillim 119, 'I have strayed like a lost sheep', and says the Jews must not despair, for despite everything Hashem has not cast them away, and the great shofar will gather the lost.
Singing of 'U'va'u ha'ovdim'.

title.en: The large tav: Esther writes for the lowly

summary.en: The large tav of 'Vatichtov' is the last letter, the end. The Mashgiach contrasts Nechemia, whose book was not counted alone because he said 'remember me for good', with Esther, who asked to be written for the generations out of complete self-nullification, and says she gave the Megillah to the lowest levels, the souls of forgetting.
Singing of 'Shebeshiflenu zachar lanu'.

The lights of the Megillah are very high but come clothed in garments. The Mashgiach says a Jew must know that all he sees in nature, history and his own life is a garment with the Ribono shel Olam inside; on Purim we dress up to say we know the world is masked, and Achashverosh hints to Hashem.

The Mashgiach brings the Midrash in which Mordechai tells Haman that his grandfather never bowed to Esav, asks how this fits with Yaakov's bowing, and answers that Yaakov bowed to the Shechinah going before him. When the Megillah is finished everything becomes clear; a Jew who sees the rulers of the world should not be frightened, for it is the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: From Hodu to Kush: the black souls

summary.en: 'From Hodu to Kush' spans every Jew, from the finest to the blackest. The Mashgiach brings the Yismach Moshe that answering a puzzling Midrash brings far-off Jews close, reads 'Are you not like the children of the Kushim to Me', and shows that the last in time, in place and in soul all equal 'bnei Kushiyim'. We are blackened by the exile, but we sing to the Ribono shel Olam, who will wash us white.
Singing of 'Hamolech mehodu ve'ad Kush'.

title.en: Achashverosh loses his vavs; Shlomo's spark

summary.en: The Megillah opens with Achashverosh, Nevuchadnetzar's partner in destruction, spelled with two vavs, then one, and at the end with none. The Mashgiach explains that Achashverosh carried a spark of Shlomo HaMelech, who slept on the day of the Beis HaMikdash's dedication; the night the king's sleep was disturbed was the repair, and from Haman's house, which he gave to Esther, the Beis HaMikdash was built.

The Mashgiach continues: according to the Midrash Haman found the treasures of the Beis HaMikdash, and from Haman's house it was rebuilt. Once Achashverosh had given the money, the holy spark went out of him, and he was left an empty shell without his vavs. Singing follows.
Singing.

The Mitzri whom Moshe killed was reincarnated as Haman. Moshe hid that salvation 'in the sand', in the weekdays, so that the weekday Yom Tov of Purim would sustain the Jews in exile. The man he struck was beating Dasan, and Amalek attacked the camp of Dan; Hashem does not allow anyone to attack even the lowest Jew, for every Jew has a hidden root.
Singing of 'Mah tishtochachi nafshi'.

title.en: The forgotten sheaf and the last letters

summary.en: Hashem has a personal field where the souls of forgetting grow. The Mashgiach ties them to the last letters of the Torah, said in the days of mourning for Moshe when halachos were forgotten, and tells the story of a beautiful Sefer Torah whose last letters showed it was written by a heretic, and the Pnei Menachem's words that a minhag Yisrael is Torah.

title.en: Esther, soul of the last letters

summary.en: Esther heads the souls of the last letters and of forgetting; even a Megillah with some blurred letters is kosher, and 'as I am lost, I am lost' equals 'and you forget a sheaf in the field'. The Mashgiach describes how the Shechinah left Esther in the house of idols until she drew the Beis HaMikdash into Shushan, entering the inner house of the King.

The Mashgiach tells of the Tzemach Tzedek, who told a Jew wishing to move to Eretz Yisrael to make Eretz Yisrael where he was. 'He raises the poor from the dust to seat them with nobles' joins Dan's Ohaliav with Yehudah's Betzalel, and there is no forgetting with olives, as Klal Yisrael is never forgotten. Tonight Yerushalayim keeps Purim, and the Jews at the seudah sing and long for Yerushalayim and draw it to themselves.

title.en: The Shechinah with Sarah and with Esther

summary.en: Bringing the Zera Kodesh, the Mashgiach explains that Mordechai told Esther not to send a substitute but to go herself, for a miracle for all generations must come from a holy place. From the Zohar on Avraham and Sarah he shows that Esther sought the Shechinah's company as Sarah had in Pharaoh's house; it left her, and returned when she 'clothed herself in royalty'. The Shechinah is with us even in Shushan.
Singing.

The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Megillah where Rabbi Eliezer rebuked a man who read 'Make known to Yerushalayim her abominations', and asks why, when Yechezkel said the same verse; he answers that Yechezkel meant to bring out Yerushalayim's merit, as the Kedushas Levi reads 'Hoy goy chotei' in praise. Purim, in Shushan, the place of hiding, reveals the hidden love of every Jew and binds him to Yerushalayim.
Singing.

title.en: The preserved wine and the secret of every Jew

summary.en: Esther reveals the hidden love of the Jews. The Mashgiach brings Bilam's 'How can I curse', Yaakov's fear of a curse, and the Targum Yonasan that angels brought Yaakov wine preserved from creation; wine is the secret, the innermost point that no sin reaches, and even the 'traitors' are blessed. Rabbi Motele of Chernobyl says Moshiach is the aspect of Mordechai, the preserved wine, and the wine of Purim is that wine.
Singing.
Singing.
Singing.

title.en: Kol haposhet yad: a time of favor

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that every moment of Purim is a great time of favor, when whoever stretches out his hand is given. Tzaddikim reading a Jew's request for material needs saw what he lacked in spirit, and one must feel like a poor man, as David HaMelech did; as much as one knows his poverty, so much is given from Heaven. Singing follows.
An interlude.
Singing of 'Vatosef Esther'.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why dates given for Moshiach were real opportunities, brings the Ba'al HaTanya's hint of 5775 in the pasuk of the extra silver used for the vavim, and connects the missing vav of the alphabetical kapitlach of Tehillim to Yidden outside the camp whom Hashem redeems.

abstract.en: Speaking before Rosh Hashanah, the Mashgiach notes that tzaddikim through the generations set dates for Moshiach, and asks why Ravina and Rav Ashi recorded in the Gemara a date that had already passed. He answers that every such date was truly an 'achishenah' time, ready for the geulah, but someone spoiled it; the final 'b'itah' date is fixed and unknown. He then tells how the Ba'al HaTanya, reading the Torah, read 'ha'elef' in the pasuk of the vavim as heh-elef, hinting at 5775. He asks why the vav is missing in the alphabetical kapitlach of Tehillim and replaced by a pei. His answer: the extra Yidden whose half-shekels went to the vavim, which protrude outside the Mishkan, are those outside the camp, like Bnei Dan whom Amalek attacked and the last pesukim of the Torah; Hashem does not forsake them, and 'Podeh Hashem' brings them back. He closes that our generation is at the end, and every small avodah is precious.

en: Every date the tzaddikim set for Moshiach was a real 'achishenah' time when he was ready to come, but someone spoiled it.
The final 'b'itah' date is fixed and unknown to anyone; Moshiach must come then.
The Ba'al HaTanya read 'ha'elef' in the pasuk of the vavim as heh-elef and said the geulah is hinted there in 5775.
The missing vav of the alphabetical kapitlach stands for the Yidden outside the camp, whose silver went to the vavim that protrude outside the Mishkan.
Hashem does not forsake those Yidden; with Moshiach they return, as the closing pei 'Podeh Hashem nefesh avadav' shows.
In our generation, at the end of the galus, Hashem does not expect much, and every small effort in learning and tefillah is precious to Him.

summary.en: Before Rosh Hashanah the Mashgiach notes that tzaddikim gave dates for Moshiach, and asks why the Gemara records a date that had already passed. He answers that each was a real 'achishenah' time spoiled by sin, while the final 'b'itah' date is unknown.

The Mashgiach tells how the Ba'al HaTanya, reading Parshas Pekudei, read 'ha'elef' as heh-elef and would not be corrected, saying the geulah is hinted in the pasuk in 5775, and how he heard this confirmed. He asks Yidden not to spoil the year and to take on resolutions before Yom Kippur.

The Mashgiach shows that the alphabetical kapitlach 34 and 25 of Tehillim skip the vav and add an extra pei at the end, brings the Divrei Yechezkel that the pei replaces the vav through atbash, and asks why the vav must be missing at all.

title.en: Moshe forgets the vavim; Bnei Dan

summary.en: Returning to the pasuk, the Mashgiach explains that Moshe forgot what he did with the extra 1,775 shekels until he was reminded that they went to the vavim, the silver hooks on the amudim, and asks why Moshe forgot. He then speaks of Bnei Dan, expelled from the camp under the Ananei HaKavod, whom Amalek attacked.

title.en: Every Yid a letter in the Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the 600,000 letters of the Torah correspond to the 600,000 souls of Klal Yisrael, and how the Chachamim counted them. He suggests that the Yidden outside the camp are in the last eight pesukim of the Torah, which have a different status.

title.en: The extra silver and the Yidden outside

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects the forgetting at Moshe's passing and the last words of the Torah with the extra Yidden beyond 600,000, whose half-shekels went to the vavim that protrude outside the Mishkan's curtains. Hashem does not forsake them, and His anger at Amalek for attacking them still burns; he adds that Dovid HaMelech, in danger with Avimelech, composed the kapitel of the 22 letters.

The Mashgiach answers his question: the vav is missing from the alphabet like the Yidden outside the camp, and the pei 'Podeh Hashem nefesh avadav' brings them back when Moshiach comes. He says our generation is the souls at the end of the Torah, and repeats that the Ba'al HaTanya's hint, also found in an earlier sefer, points to a time about 200 years after him.

title.en: Small avodah in the last generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach says our generation needs emunah and teshuvah, brings the Arizal's words to Rav Chaim Vital that the later generations are smaller, and says that today any small, hard-won avodah is precious to Hashem. He urges using the remaining days before Yom Kippur, and closes with the hope of meeting next year in Yerushalayim.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach shows how on Purim every end turns into a beginning and every judgment into kindness, and calls on Jews to ask at the seudah for Yerushalayim and the redemption.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with matanos l'evyonim and the theme of forgetting: Haman saw 7 Adar as the day of Moshe's passing, but it is also his birthday, so for those bound to Hashem an end becomes a beginning and the Megillah is a hope for those who are far. Through two statements of R' Yirmiyah he explains the final letters mantzepach, a limit of din that turns into chesed, and Purim breaking the walls of Yerushalayim. He speaks of wine and kiddush, of leaving a portion for the sitra achra, and of ad delo yada. Later he discusses Mordechai's milk, Haman's descendants in Bnei Brak, the hidden miracle, the fast on Pesach and leil shimurim, Mordechai as the root of unity, and Esther's cry. He closes with a story of the Apter Rav and a call to ask for Yerushalayim at the seudah.

en: Haman knew that Moshe died on 7 Adar but not that he was born then; for those bound to Hashem, who has no end, an end turns into a new beginning.
The final letters mantzepach are letters of din when they close a word, but in the days of Moshiach the limit will be removed, as in the closed mem in the middle of the word in Yeshayahu.
Some nourishment must be left to the sitra achra, and this explains why Haman too receives a small portion on Purim through ad delo yada.
The whole miracle of Purim came about through Achashverosh not knowing, and this is the source of Rava's ad delo yada.
Purim reveals ein od milvado: a Jew who holds to it sees Hashem in everything, and no sorcery or evil power can touch him.
The Purim seudah is the greatest eis ratzon of the year, when Hashem asks Klal Yisrael what they request, and one should ask to see Yerushalayim and the third Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Matanos l'evyonim and the day of forgetting

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with matanos l'evyonim on Purim and explains that the evyon is in the aspect of forgetting. Haman thought 7 Adar, the day of Moshe's passing when halachos were forgotten, was a day of forgetting, but it is also Moshe's birthday, a day of remembering, so on Purim all the merits of Jews are remembered.
Singing.

title.en: The end that becomes a beginning

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haman saw Moshe's passing as an end, like the end of a straight line, but Jews bound to Hashem are like a circle, where the end turns into a beginning. The Megillah is therefore a great hope for those who are far.

title.en: The Megillah opens with drawing the far near

summary.en: Like an author who states his theme at the start, the Megillah opens with Achashverosh's feast, where, the Gemara says, he gave precedence to those from afar. The Mashgiach explains that Hashem carries out His plan through anyone, and that the theme of the Megillah is drawing near those who are far.
An interlude.

title.en: Mantzepach: letters of redemption and of din

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects two statements of R' Yirmiyah in the name of R' Chiya bar Abba: a town near Yerushalayim reads the Megillah like it, and the final letters mantzepach. Inside a word these letters are chesed and redemption, at its end a limit of din; in the days of Moshiach the closed mem will stand in the middle of a word and Yerushalayim will have no walls, which Purim already brings about.

title.en: R' Yirmiyah, R' Chiya bar Abba and Shushan Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains R' Yirmiyah as a soul of churban and R' Chiya bar Abba as the aspect of Purim, yesod abba; joined together in Maseches Megillah, the dinim turn into chesed. He speaks of Hashem's Name being incomplete until Amalek is gone, of Shushan Purim breaking through the wall, of malchus spreading on Purim, and ends with the hope that the Name become complete.

On the passuk of the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine, the Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the Jews then made kiddush and sang praises. Wine, seventy in gematria, is the Name Havayah with dam, so wine leads to blood, while the Jews' kiddush draws from the Name Havayah.

title.en: Leaving a portion for the sitra achra

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Bnei Yissaschar on not eating matzah on erev Pesach, the Chasam Sofer on why thirty-nine lashes are given instead of forty, and the Arizal, all teaching that some nourishment must be left to the sitra achra. On this he explains ad delo yada: Haman too receives a small portion, through a mistake.

title.en: Haman's spark and the honor of Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Magen Avraham that kiddush is not made in the first hour of Friday night, ruled by Maadim, the planet the Maharal ties to Haman. By leaving him that spark the Jews gave Haman something he had to repay, so he became subordinate to Mordechai. He concludes that all of creation, even the sitra achra, serves Hashem's honor, and Haman's merit was only to fall as a kiddush Hashem.
Singing.

title.en: The Megillah's opening and Mordechai's milk

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the opening words of the Megillah hold the whole Megillah, v'nahafoch, Achashverosh being a changeable king. He brings the Midrash that Mordechai nursed Esther and the Mishnah that male milk is tahor, and explains that milk is blood transformed, din turned into chesed; a man's milk comes from Abba, a higher sweetening, and from it Esther drew.

title.en: Mordechai and the transformation of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Haman as the etz hada'as and Mordechai as mor dror, musk that is permitted because it has been transformed. The word Megillah with its letters filled out equals 'kulo hafach lavan'; on Purim Jews draw from the highest source, and he brings the Arizal that Purim is higher than Shabbos and Yom Tov.

title.en: Haman at Esther's feast and Bnei Brak

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that through the holiness of Esther's feast Haman merited descendants who taught Torah in Bnei Brak, R' Shmuel bar Shilas. He shows that Zeresh is mentioned three times together with Haman's friends and a fourth time with his wise men, when she separated from the klipah.

title.en: The power of the seudah at night

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the seudah, after the Megillah, matanos l'evyonim and mishloach manos, as the greatest eis ratzon of the year, and brings that tzaddikim held the main seudah at night. He ties Yitzchak's blessing 'mishmanei ha'aretz' and R' Shaman bar Abba, the first sage named in Maseches Megillah, to the oil of yesod abba, and says one must ask Hashem at the seudah.

title.en: Why Haman knew only of Moshe's passing

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Haman knew that Moshe died on 7 Adar but not that he was born then. He answers that at Moshe's birth the hidden light was revealed, a light hidden away from the wicked, so Haman had no access to it.

title.en: Ad delo yada and the hidden miracle

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks where Rava learns that one must drink ad delo yada. He brings the Zohar and the Koznitzer Maggid that Esther sent a sheida in her place, and asks how Achashverosh never noticed. Answering that what Hashem wants hidden is not known, he explains that the whole miracle came through not knowing, and the sheida's name with its letters filled out equals ad delo yada.
An interlude.

title.en: The fast on Pesach and the sorcery of Haman's sons

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses when Mordechai and the Jews fasted, according to Rashi and according to the Midrash, and brings the Midrash Tehillim that Haman's sons were sorcerers who worked against Mordechai. He brings the Gemara of Zeiri's donkey to show that crossing water annuls sorcery.

title.en: Leil shimurim and ein od milvado

summary.en: The Mashgiach reconciles the opinions about the fast through the Gemara on the four cups: on the night of Pesach, leil shimurim protects against sorcery, while on the night before, Mordechai needed to cross the water. He ties Purim, thirty days before Pesach, to the power of leil shimurim, and concludes with R' Chanina's ein od milvado, which Purim reveals.
An interlude.

title.en: Mordechai Bilshan, the root of unity

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Mordechai is Pesachyah, appointed over the kinnim, who could mix languages. He contrasts Amalek, the head of separation, with Mordechai, who comes from the root of unity above all languages, explains why he dealt with taharah, and ends with 'v'dover shalom l'chol zar'o'.

title.en: Esther's cry in the house of idols

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Esther cried out in the house of idols for later generations, when the whole world will be like a house of idols. He brings a mashal from the Divrei Shlomo of a child who fell into mud, the Midrash on Kayin, and the Beis Avraham, on a Jew's claim before Hashem.

title.en: A planting of simchah on Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Rebbi planted on Purim, a planting of simchah, a wedding house for his son. He speaks of the joy of a chosson on Purim as a planting of joy for all worlds, bound with the joy of Yerushalayim.
An interlude.

title.en: The Apter Rav and the Rebbe R' Elimelech

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells, in the name of the Apter Rav, of a Simchas Torah at the Rebbe R' Elimelech, when a harsh decree that tears and Torah had not moved was annulled through the joy of Jews, and the Apter Rav was asked in Heaven what he wished to see.

The Mashgiach says the Purim seudah is the greatest eis ratzon, when Hashem asks Klal Yisrael what they request, and one should ask to see Yerushalayim and the third Beis HaMikdash and bind oneself to the Jews of Yerushalayim. He explains that Shushan Purim came not through the lot but because Hashem saw how Jews celebrate Purim.
Singing.

title.en: Esther's maidens and the word Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Esther counted the days through her seven maidens, and the Targum that the Shabbos maiden had a name meaning rest. Saying the word Shabbos draws holiness, so Esther would call it out aloud, and Hashem gave her in return a weekday with the holiness of Shabbos, Purim.
Singing.

The Mashgiach says that now is the Neilah of Purim, greater than the Neilah of Yom Kippur, and that Shabbos and Yerushalayim are one. He calls on those present to bind themselves to Yerushalayim, take hold of the king's scepter as Esther did, and ask Hashem for Klal Yisrael.
Singing.

oneLiner.en: At the seudah of Purim Meshulash, the Mashgiach connects Mordechai's handful of the Omer with Haman's fall and ends by teaching that every Jew, wherever he is, is a shaliach of the Ribono shel Olam.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach speaks at the Purim seudah of a year in which Purim falls on Shabbos. He opens with the joy of Purim, the tzaddik at the head of the simcha, and the wine and customs of the seudah. He speaks of the kedushah of the Kosel Maaravi and of the three-day Purim. He then turns to Haman finding Mordechai with the korban of the Omer on the second day of Pesach: the first day of the count holds the root of all fifty days, which he connects with the fifty-amah gallows. He speaks of Yaakov bowing when he met Esav, of Moshiach ben David and the spark of Moshiach, of seeing the Mikdash from afar, and closes with the Tanya's teaching that a Jew in chutz la'aretz who does mitzvos draws down the Shechinah, so every Jew is Hashem's shaliach.

en: The Mashgiach discusses the year in which Purim falls on Shabbos and three days are needed, with the Megillah read on Friday in Yerushalayim.
Haman found Mordechai occupied with the korban of the Omer on the second day of Pesach, the first day of the count, which holds the root of all fifty days.
When Yaakov went to meet Esav, the Mashgiach explains, his bowing was directed to the Shechinah.
Citing the Tanya, the Mashgiach teaches that a Jew in chutz la'aretz who learns, davens, gives tzedakah and does mitzvos draws the Shechinah down and breaks the power of the sitra achra.
Every Jew is on a shlichus of the Ribono shel Olam; one need not be a Lubavitcher to be a shaliach.

summary.en: The opening of the seudah.

title.en: The joy of Purim and the tzaddik

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the joy of Purim and of the tzaddik who stands at the head of the simcha, and of drinking wine at the seudah.
The Mashgiach mentions customs connected with the seudah, among them a custom of Gur.

title.en: The Kosel Maaravi and Purim on Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the kedushah of the Beis Hamikdash and of the Kosel Maaravi, a kedushah that breaks through barriers. He then discusses the year in which Purim falls on Shabbos, when three days are needed and the Megillah is read on Friday in Yerushalayim.

title.en: Mordechai's kometz and the fifty days

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the shekalim, and of Haman coming with the horse and finding Mordechai with the korban of the Omer on the second day of Pesach. He explains that the first day of the count is the root of all fifty days, and connects it with Haman hanged on a gallows fifty amos high.
The Mashgiach speaks of Yaakov and his household bowing when they met Esav, and explains that Yaakov's bowing was directed to the Shechinah. He mentions Mordechai in this connection.

title.en: Moshiach ben David and the hidden spark

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Moshiach ben David, bringing the Or HaChaim on Moshiach ben David and Moshiach ben Yosef. He then speaks of Balak and of the spark of Moshiach that was hidden in him.
The Mashgiach speaks of the birth of Yosef and Yaakov's stance toward Esav, and mentions tzaddikim of later generations, among them Rabbi Yoel.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach speaks of seeing the place of the Mikdash from Tzofim, and asks what counts as seeing when people see to different distances. He mentions the Luchos that Yoshiyahu hid, and says that when Moshiach comes Jews will see far.
The Mashgiach returns to the Megillah and to Esther, mentions Rabbi Yoel, and speaks of reaching down to the lowest levels.
An interlude.

The Mashgiach brings the Tanya that a Jew in chutz la'aretz who learns, davens and does mitzvos draws the Shechinah down and breaks the sitra achra, and concludes that every Jew is a shaliach of the Ribono shel Olam. He closes with a brachah for emunah, yiras Shamayim and ahavah, and that all Jews come to Eretz Yisroel.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach explains how the hidden root of every Jew, above all sin and failure, is revealed on Purim through Mordechai's refusal to bow and Esther's pure mesiras nefesh.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Purim as a time when simcha brings salvation, and with Yaakov Avinu, who laid the ground for Chanukah and Purim and left his holiness with the Jews in exile. From Rabbi Tzadok HaKohen he teaches that a stumble is a sign that one can rise to the highest level in that very thing: Shushan failed at Achashveirosh's feast, which imitated the Beis HaMikdash, yet the Mikdash was rebuilt with Haman's money, and his own generation can rise the same way. He explains why Mordechai could not bow, though Yaakov bowed to Esav: Mordechai brought the hidden Shechinah into the open. Achashveirosh's bigdei kehunah meant to arouse the sale of Yosef, but awakened the root of Israel above sin. He describes Esther's pure mesiras nefesh, the Megillah's ruach hakodesh proven by the Jews' acceptance, Esther's seven maidens and Shabbos, and the holy wine of Purim.

en: Purim is a time when, through simcha, great salvations can be drawn down for the Jewish people.
A stumble is a sign that one can reach the greatest elevation in that very matter: from Shushan's failure came the rebuilding of the Beis HaMikdash, and the same holds for his generation.
Mordechai could not bow to Haman, because he carried the level that brings the hidden Shechinah into the open.
Klal Yisrael has a hidden root above all sin, which Haman did not know and which is revealed on Purim.
Esther's mesiras nefesh was pure, like Avraham's at the Akeidah: she was ready to be remembered in disgrace forever, only to save the Jews.
The strongest proof that the Megillah was said with ruach hakodesh is that the Jews accepted it; prophecy remains with Klal Yisrael as a whole.
The wine of Purim is the wine preserved since Creation, the inner point of every Jew, and it prepares for the four cups of Pesach.
